description:
card.rs:198-219 (ContactCardFilterCondition) and card.rs:315-322 (ContactCardComparator) both carry a '# Excluded from extras preservation' rustdoc section explaining (1) why these types deliberately have no 'extra' catch-all, (2) the IETF-track path forward (draft-ietf-jmap-metadata, bd JMAP-06zp), (3) the pre-IETF escape (Value-tree or fork). README.md §'Filter extensibility' carries the same message at user-facing-doc level. Both link to bd JMAP-lbdy.

A future contributor who sees 'every other type has extras, why don't these' will (a) try to add extras and (b) be redirected to the spec-conformant alternative without breaking the type. The rustdoc-as-defense pattern is the right move here — a comment that says 'don't do X' next to the type that would tempt X is worth more than a workspace AGENTS.md rule that the contributor might not read.

Do not delete these doc sections to 'shorten the rustdoc'. The length is the point — it documents a non-obvious decision and saves the next contributor (or future-you) from re-litigating it.
title: GOOD: pre-emptive Filter-extensibility rustdoc + README explaining the exclusion
